Budget = 85,000 JPY/month is OUR ESTIMATE (not official): the JASSO average with about 20,000 less rent, assuming a university dormitory or regional city. Comfortable = 167,000 JPY/month is Hitotsubashi ICS's Tokyo estimate of 2,000,000 JPY/year for housing and living, divided by 12. None include tuition.

student_visa.name: Status of residence 'Student' (Ryugaku); Long Term Stay visa issued on a Certificate of Eligibility (COE)

fees.label: Visa fee, Indian nationals (single or multiple entry), via VFS India
Extension of period of stay in Japan, 1-year period, at counter (from 1 Oct 2026; 27,000 online)

proof_of_funds.text: No fixed national amount. The COE application requires a statement of who will pay expenses (expense support statement) and scholarship certificates where applicable (ISA 'Student' page: https://www.moj.go.jp/isa/applications/status/student.html). University guidance typically asks for a bank balance covering one year of tuition and living costs. Tokyo Metropolitan University states a minimum of 1 million JPY (1.5 million recommended); Tsukuba asks for a support letter, the supporter's bank balance certificate and an income certificate. Some universities require coverage until graduation for self-funded students. Expect roughly 1.5 to 2.5 million JPY for a national-university year (535,800 tuition plus living); more for private MBAs.

work_during_study.text: Paid work needs 'Permission to Engage in Activity Other than That Permitted' (no fee). Limits: 28 hours per week during term and up to 8 hours per day during long vacations. New arrivals can apply at airports that issue residence cards, right after landing. Work at adult-entertainment businesses is prohibited, and no work is allowed during a leave of absence. Most part-time jobs need some Japanese.

post_study_work.name: Designated Activities (continued job hunting after graduation), then 'Engineer/Specialist in Humanities/International Services' work status
post_study_work.text: There is no open post-study work permit. Graduates who started job hunting while enrolled can switch to Designated Activities for job hunting with a recommendation letter from their university (ISA). The status is normally 6 months, renewable once, so up to 1 year (UTokyo GSFS guidance: https://www.k.u-tokyo.ac.jp/en/international/student_support/job_hunting/). Working legally requires an employer job offer and a change to a work status such as Engineer/Specialist in Humanities/International Services, with periods of 5 years, 3 years, 1 year or 3 months (https://www.moj.go.jp/isa/applications/status/gijinkoku.html). J-Find (since April 2023) allows up to 2 years for eligible graduates of top-ranked universities. Japanese ability strongly affects job prospects outside English-speaking tech and foreign-capital firms.

pr_pathway.text: Highly Skilled Professional (HSP) points route: 70+ points qualifies for HSP status; PR possible after 3 years at 70+ points or 1 year at 80+ points. A master's degree and a high salary add points. General route: in principle 10 years of continuous residence, including 5+ years on a work status. Revised ISA PR guidelines (1 Oct 2026, for applications filed from 1 Apr 2027) add: household income above the Japanese average for the same household size, projected pension contributions, Japanese at B1 level (HSP holders exempt), and holding the maximum period of stay. The PR application fee rises from 10,000 to 200,000 JPY from 1 Oct 2026.

recent_changes.title: Residence permission fees raised (change of status, extension of stay, permanent residence)
recent_changes.who_affected: All foreign residents filing change-of-status, extension or PR applications received on or after 1 Oct 2026
recent_changes.impact: The old flat fee was 6,000 JPY at the counter (5,500 online). Fees now depend on the period of stay granted: 10,000 (3 months or less), 33,000 (1 year), 64,000 (3 years) or 75,000 (5 years or more) at the counter, with lower online rates. PR rises from 10,000 to 200,000. An Indian student pays more for each visa extension and for the student-to-work switch: roughly 33,000 to 75,000 JPY each instead of 6,000. This is a small but real ROI cost.

recent_changes.title: Permanent residence guidelines tightened (income, pension, Japanese B1, maximum period of stay)
recent_changes.who_affected: PR applicants filing from 1 Apr 2027; the income requirement also applies to applications filed from 1 Apr 2026
recent_changes.impact: PR becomes harder for typical graduates: you need household income above the Japanese average, a pension record, Japanese at B1 level unless you are HSP, and from April 2027 generally the 5-year maximum period of stay. The HSP 70-point/3-year and 80-point/1-year fast tracks remain. Long-term settlement value is lower for mid-salary graduates.

recent_changes.title: Visa issuance fees raised about fivefold (single entry ~15,000 JPY, multiple ~30,000 JPY)
recent_changes.who_affected: Visa applicants of most nationalities; VFS India still lists INR 500 for Indian nationals
recent_changes.impact: Little or no impact on Indian students: VFS India still lists a 500 INR visa fee (single or multiple), and news reports say the Embassy kept the Indian rate. The MOFA notice (https://www.mofa.go.jp/j_info/visit/visa/procedure/pagewe_000001_00391.html) returned 403 to us; the 15,000/30,000 figures come from that notice as quoted in search results.

check.note: The stored source does not contain this figure and the official notice could not be read, so it is not confirmed.

recent_changes.title: Extra documents for Engineer/Specialist in Humanities/International Services applications with Category 3/4 employers (e.g. CEFR B2 proof for language roles)
recent_changes.who_affected: Graduates switching to a work status with smaller or newer employers (Category 3 and 4)
recent_changes.impact: More paperwork and scrutiny when moving from student to work status at small firms. Roles that mainly use language skills must show B2-level proof, which makes the job-to-visa step slightly harder.

recent_changes.title: Tohoku University: higher tuition for new international undergraduate and master's students from AY2027 (reported 900,000 JPY/yr); need-based exemption ends after AY2026

The 900,000 figure comes from news reports, not that page. Reported effect: about 70% more tuition for students who do not get the scholarship.

policy_volatility.evidence: Changes in the last 24 months: residence fees restructured (Oct 2026), visa fees raised fivefold for most nationalities (Jul 2026), PR guidelines revised twice in 2026, extra work-visa documents (Apr 2026), and separate higher international tuition announced at Tohoku and Tsukuba for 2027. The core Student/COE framework and the 28-hour work rule did not change.

psw_uncertainty.evidence: There is no guaranteed open post-study permit. Job hunting is limited to Designated Activities (6 months, renewable once, max about 1 year) and needs a university recommendation. Staying requires an employer offer and a change of work status. Japanese language often decides employability.

work_restrictions.evidence: Study-time work is capped at 28 h/week (8 h/day in vacations) and needs permission, and most part-time jobs need Japanese. After study, work is employer-sponsored, and Category 3/4 employers now face extra documents, including B2 language proof for language roles.

funds_burden.evidence: No fixed statutory amount. Universities typically ask for a bank balance covering one year of tuition and living (e.g. TMU: 1M JPY minimum, 1.5M recommended). National-university tuition of 535,800 JPY keeps the proof amount low relative to the UK, US or Australia.

recent_adverse.evidence: In the last 12 months: visa extension and student-to-work fees rose from 6,000 to 33,000-75,000 JPY (Oct 2026), PR rules were tightened (income above the Japanese average, B1 Japanese, from 2027), and some national universities announced higher international tuition from 2027. Visa fees for Indians were left unchanged.

CS.basis: Official MHLW 2025 Basic Survey on Wage Structure, all industries, both sexes, master's (graduate school) holders, scheduled monthly earnings (所定内給与) x 12, EXCLUDING bonuses and overtime. Low = new graduate master's 299.0k/month. Mid = master's holders aged 25-29, 335.0k/month. High = master's holders aged 30-34, 406.1k/month, an upper proxy for strong offers. These are not occupation-specific. Japanese firms usually also pay bonuses, so real annual pay is often higher; these figures are conservative.
CS.source_name: MHLW Basic Survey on Wage Structure 2025 (令和7年賃金構造基本統計調査), tables 10 (new graduates) and 3 (by education and age)
CS.period: June 2025 monthly scheduled earnings, annualised x12

DS.basis: Same as CS: MHLW 2025 master's new graduates (299.0k), master's aged 25-29 (335.0k) and 30-34 (406.1k) monthly scheduled earnings x 12, all industries, bonuses excluded. No official data-science-specific entry wage was found.
DS.source_name: MHLW Basic Survey on Wage Structure 2025 (令和7年賃金構造基本統計調査), tables 10 and 3
DS.period: June 2025 monthly scheduled earnings, annualised x12

MBA.basis: MBA graduates usually have 2+ years of prior experience (Hitotsubashi requires it), so we use older age bands of MHLW 2025 master's holders: low = aged 25-29 (335.0k/month), mid = 30-34 (406.1k), high = 35-39 (466.6k), each x 12, all industries, bonuses excluded. This is a proxy; no official MBA-specific wage statistic was found.
MBA.source_name: MHLW Basic Survey on Wage Structure 2025 (令和7年賃金構造基本統計調査), table 3 (by education and age)
MBA.period: June 2025 monthly scheduled earnings, annualised x12

tax.basis: OECD Taxing Wages 2025 data for Japan, single person with no children: average rate of income tax (national + local/resident) plus employee social security contributions = 20.56% of gross at 67% of the average wage (gross 3,821,036 JPY) and 22.65% at 100% (5,703,038 JPY). Employee SSC alone is 14.7%. Entry salaries here (3.6-4.9M JPY) sit between these points, so we use about 21% as an ESTIMATE. Resident tax is charged on the prior year's income, so first-year deductions are lower in practice.

checklist: Shortlist English-taught programmes and check the current year's application guide for fees and intake (April/October)
Apply and pass the entrance exam or interview; pay the exam fee (often 30,000 JPY)
Prepare proof of funds: sponsor letter, bank balance certificate covering about 1 year of tuition and living, and the sponsor's income certificate
University applies for your Certificate of Eligibility (COE) at the Immigration Services Agency (about 3-8 weeks)
Receive the COE and apply for the student visa through VFS Global in India (INR 500 fee + INR 800 service charge) with the original COE
Pay the admission fee (about 282,000 JPY at national universities) and first-semester tuition; apply for fee exemption or scholarships
At the arrival airport, receive your residence card and apply for part-time work permission (28 h/week)
Register your address at the city office within 14 days and enrol in National Health Insurance and the National Pension (student deferral available)
Open a bank account and get a phone; start Japanese lessons early because they matter for jobs and PR
Start job hunting before graduation; get the university recommendation for Designated Activities (job hunting) or switch to a work visa once you have an offer
